concerns.text: The plan relies on a paired t‑test for per‑document log‑perplexity differences but does not specify any check for the normality of the difference distribution; if normality is violated the test’s Type I error rate is uncontrolled.

Multiple outcome metrics (perplexity, QA accuracy, latency, memory) are reported, yet the plan treats only perplexity as a primary hypothesis and provides no correction for multiple comparisons, risking inflated false‑positive rates across the other metrics.

Power analysis is performed only for the perplexity difference (Cohen’s d = 0.8, N≈30). No power calculation is provided for QA accuracy or memory‑footprint differences, which may be under‑powered given the same test set size.

The plan states FR‑007 ‘Evaluate on a downstream long‑context QA task (HotpotQA subset)’ but cites the dataset URL `https://huggingface.co/datasets/llamaindex/long-qa`. The cited dataset (Long‑QA) is a distinct resource from the original HotpotQA benchmark. This mismatch creates ambiguity about which dataset will actually be used and whether it satisfies the long‑context requirement (≥ 32 k tokens). Clarify the exact dataset name, ensure the chosen dataset provides contexts of the required length, and update the citation to match the dataset that will be used for evaluation.

The plan uses a paired t‑test on per‑document log‑perplexities (see ‘perform a **paired t‑test** on per‑document perplexities (FR‑003‑FR‑008)’). A paired t‑test assumes the differences are approximately normally distributed. The plan does not include any check (e.g., Shapiro‑Wilk test or visual inspection) to verify this assumption, nor does it specify a fallback non‑parametric test (e.g., Wilcoxon signed‑rank) if normality is violated. This methodological omission could invalidate the claimed statistical significance (SC‑003).
